hypothesis: Which commonly used price-only rule, if any, beats equal-weight buy-and-hold on the same universe after costs?

benchmark.label: Equal-weight continuous hold
benchmark.rule: Buy every asset once at equal weight and never rebalance.

strategies.label: Momentum 12m (current allocator)
strategies.rule: Hold the top N by trailing 12-month return, equal weight.

strategies.label: Momentum 12-1
strategies.rule: Top N by 12-month return excluding the latest month, equal weight.

strategies.label: Dual momentum
strategies.rule: Top N by 12-month return, but an asset with a negative 12-month return stays cash.

strategies.label: Time-series momentum
strategies.rule: Hold every asset with a positive 12-month return at 1/universe each; rest cash.

strategies.label: Trend: price > 200-day SMA
strategies.rule: Hold every asset trading above its 200-day average at 1/universe each; rest cash.

strategies.label: MA distance (21d / 200d)
strategies.rule: Top N by 21-day average relative to 200-day average, equal weight.

strategies.label: MA distance + sell buffer
strategies.rule: MA distance, but keep a holding until it drops out of the top 5 (turnover control).
strategies.source: Variant of MA distance; buffer width fixed in advance, counted as an extra trial

strategies.label: Low volatility
strategies.rule: Top N lowest trailing one-year daily volatility, equal weight.

strategies.label: Short-term reversal
strategies.rule: Top N by worst last-month return, equal weight.

strategies.label: Technical blend + trend filter
strategies.rule: Average rank of 12-1 momentum, MA distance and low volatility; must also be above the 200-day SMA.
strategies.source: Composite of the rules above (a combination, not a new search axis)

strategies.label: Quality (profitability, cash, leverage)
strategies.rule: Top N by average rank of ROE, net margin, FCF margin and low debt/equity from the latest knowable fiscal year.
strategies.source: Novy-Marx 2013 / Asness et al. quality family

strategies.label: Revenue growth
strategies.rule: Top N by latest knowable fiscal-year revenue growth.

strategies.label: Quality + momentum
strategies.rule: Top N by average rank of quality score and 12-1 momentum.

strategies.label: Quality, only above 200-day SMA
strategies.rule: Top N quality names, restricted to those trading above their 200-day average; empty slots stay cash.
strategies.source: Quality with a Faber trend filter

strategies.label: Buy only strong quality (rest cash)
strategies.rule: Hold a name at 1/universe only while its quality score is in the universe's top quartile; otherwise that slot is cash.
strategies.source: Quality with an absolute-style entry gate; threshold fixed in advance

strategies.label: Strong quality only (equal weight)
strategies.rule: Split capital equally across the names whose quality score is in the top quartile.
strategies.source: Quality top-quartile basket; threshold fixed in advance

notes: Monthly decisions; fills at the next common session open; one-way cost on turnover.
16 rules were compared; the deflated Sharpe corrects for that search.
Universe is a fixed, curated watchlist of surviving large caps (survivorship-biased) and has been inspected before; dip-buying rules look better there than they would on a point-in-time index.

Fundamental rules use SEC CompanyFacts by filing date plus one day, from the latest fiscal year (up to ~18 months old); value ratios are excluded because split-adjusted prices cannot be divided by as-reported per-share data.
Prices are provider-adjusted; dividends, taxes and real-world fills are unverified.
